I've written the recommendation below. I have fit nothing and inspected no data. Every check in the memo is marked as planned.

**Bottom line**

- **The trial already answers the board's question.** The 12 report towns were picked by a random draw, so comparing them with the 12 control towns over March 2025 to February 2026 measures the effect of mailing the reports. Primary design: compare the two groups of towns, adjusting for each household's own use the year before. Measure uncertainty at the town level, using the random draw itself (randomization inference).
- **The analyst's before/after plan should not be the primary analysis.** The July 2025 drought order, seasonal patterns and any trend would all be counted as effects of the reports. A comparison against the control towns removes that problem.
- **Don't control for rebate sign-up.** Sign-ups happened after the reports started and were higher in report towns, so they are probably part of how the reports work. Adjusting for them would strip out part of the effect and could add bias. Report rebate sign-up as its own outcome instead.
- **The standard errors will not be tiny.** The random draw assigned 24 towns, not 2.1 million reads, so the effective sample is 12 towns against 12. With that few towns, uncertainty should come from the random draw itself or from a small-sample correction, not from default standard errors.
- **The result covers the 24 trial towns only.** Extending it to all 58 towns is a separate question that this trial cannot answer on its own.

**File: `household-report-trial/causal-design.md`**

```markdown
# Causal design: monthly home water-use reports, 24-town trial

Pre-estimation design memo, written 2026-11-12. No data have been inspected; all
facts come from the project description, and every diagnostic below is planned,
not performed. Sources: see §8.

## 1. Decision and requested estimand

**Result:** the requested effect is **plausibly identified** by the town-level
random assignment. Primary design: a cluster-randomized intention-to-treat (ITT)
comparison of the 12 report towns with the 12 control towns. It adjusts for each
household's pre-period use to improve precision, and it uses randomization
inference at the town level. The proposed household before/after comparison is
not an identifying design for this target (§5).

- **Requested causal question:** the intervention is mailing a monthly
  neighbor-comparison report to every household in a town, starting March 2025.
  The comparator is no new mailing. The outcome is metered household water use.
  The population is households in the 24 smart-meter trial towns. Time zero is
  the first mailing in March 2025, and the horizon is 12 months (Mar 2025–Feb 2026).
  The effect is a difference in means. The decision it informs is whether the
  report program cuts use, as asked by the board. A rollout decision is assumed
  but not stated (§9).
- **Requested estimand:** the ITT of town assignment to mailed reports. It is the
  difference in mean monthly household water use over Mar 2025–Feb 2026 between
  two scenarios for the trial-town households: all their towns receive the
  mailings, versus none do. The primary scale is the absolute difference
  (assumed unit: gallons per household per month). A secondary scale is the
  percent difference relative to the control-arm mean. Each household carries
  equal weight. This is an effect of *mailing*, not of reading the reports;
  reading is unrecorded, so there is no receipt/reading effect to estimate.
  Within-town spillovers (neighbors talking, local news) are part of this
  town-level policy effect.
- **Design status for that estimand:** `plausibly identified`. Assignment was a
  random draw of 12 of 24 towns. Everyone in a report town was mailed, with no
  opt-out, so assignment and the intervention coincide. Outcomes come from
  meters for every household. The drought order and other region-wide events
  hit both arms and do not confound a randomized comparison. Gate: the
  randomization record (procedure, any stratification or re-draws, and any
  towns swapped after the draw) must be confirmed before estimation.
- **Supported alternative estimands (separate; none replaces the target):**
  1. *All-58-towns effect:* **not identified** by this trial. The 24 trial
     towns were chosen because they have smart meters, not at random. Carrying
     the result to the other 34 towns needs transport assumptions about effect
     modifiers and support.
  2. *Effect of reading the reports:* **not identified**, because reading is
     unrecorded.
  3. *Effect "not via rebate":* a mediation target needing specialist
     assumptions. It is not part of this memo.
  4. *Rebate sign-up:* an ITT on rebate sign-up is identified as a secondary
     outcome.
- **Recommendation-changing condition:** suppose the randomization record shows
  that the draw was not followed, for example towns swapped or the draw
  repeated until it looked balanced without recording it. Then status becomes
  `conditional`, and the fallback difference-in-differences (DiD) design, with
  its parallel-trends assumption, takes over. Estimation should wait only for
  the randomization record and the data definitions in §9.

Sources: Hernán and Robins (2020) on ITT and randomization.

## 2. Design and data inventory

| Fact | Known/assumed/unknown | Evidence/source | Implication/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 trial towns chosen because they have smart meters, out of 58 | Known | Partner description | Target is the 24-town population; extending to 58 towns is a separate estimand |
| A random draw assigned 12 of the 24 towns to reports | Known (procedure details unknown) | Partner description | Identifies the ITT; obtain the draw record, seed/method and any strata |
| Simple complete randomization, no strata or pairs | Assumed | None | If stratified or paired, inference and the estimator must respect strata |
| Assignment unit is the town; towns are ≥10 miles apart | Known | Partner description | Inference at town level; between-town spillover plausibly small |
| Every household in report towns mailed monthly from March 2025; no opt-out | Known | Partner description | Assignment = intervention; no noncompliance in mailing to model |
| Mail actually delivered (returns, bad addresses) | Unknown | None | Part of the policy as implemented; record the return rate descriptively |
| Who read the reports | Unknown (not recorded) | Partner description | Reading effect not identified; not needed for ITT |
| Control towns got nothing new | Known | Partner description | Confirm no utility conservation messaging that differed by arm |
| Same report content and frequency all year | Assumed | None | If content changed (e.g., drought messaging after July), the treatment is a time-varying package; record versions |
| First mailing date relative to March meter reads | Unknown | None | Defines whether March 2025 reads are pre- or post-treatment |
| Monthly meter reads for every household, Mar 2023–Feb 2026, ~2.1M reads | Known | Partner description | 24 pre-months, 12 post-months; ~58k households implied (approximate) |
| Estimated or missing reads, meter replacements, read-date drift | Unknown | None | Profile; flag estimated reads; define the monthly outcome on consumption days |
| Household size, lot size from billing records | Known (measurement date unknown) | Partner description | Use only if measured before March 2025; otherwise exclude or use the pre-period snapshot |
| Account turnover (move-ins/outs) during the trial | Unknown | None | Defines the cohort and outcome missingness (§4) |
| Drought order limiting lawn watering in all 58 towns from July 2025 | Known | Partner description | Common shock to both arms; not a confounder of the randomized contrast, but it shapes the conditions the effect is measured under |
| Drought enforcement uniform across towns | Assumed | None | Town-specific enforcement intensity is a chance-imbalance risk with 12 per arm |
| Rebate sign-ups occurred during the trial, higher in report towns | Known | Partner description | Post-treatment, likely a mediator; do not adjust; secondary outcome |
| Whether reports promoted the rebate | Unknown | None | If yes, the rebate pathway is explicitly part of the intervention |
| Other town-specific events in 2025 (rate changes, main breaks, local campaigns) | Unknown | None | Planned leave-one-town-out sensitivity; inventory events |
| Regional media coverage reaching control towns | Unknown | None | Would attenuate the contrast (interference); ask |

No data were inspected. Implied field roles: town ID (cluster, assignment
unit), arm (assigned at randomization), account/premise ID, read date and
consumption days, consumption (outcome), estimated-read flag, household size
and lot size (baseline covariates once timing is confirmed), and account
start/end dates (cohort and missingness). Also rebate sign-up date (secondary
outcome; not an adjuster) and the mailing log (dates and returns). Required
additional data: the randomization record, report content versions, and
town-level event and enforcement notes.

## 3. Causal structure and adjustment

Edge list (time-indexed; t0 = March 2025):

- `Rand -> A` : the random draw determines town arm A. No other node causes A.
- `A -> Mail -> Read(U) -> Behavior -> Y_post` : the main pathway; Read is
  unobserved.
- `A -> Mail -> Rebate -> Fixtures -> Y_post` : a rebate pathway (mediator).
- `U_hh (conservation-mindedness, unobserved) -> Rebate`, `U_hh -> Y_pre`,
  `U_hh -> Y_post`.
- `HHsize, Lot -> Y_pre, Y_post` (pre-treatment, if measured before t0).
- `Town characteristics (climate, demographics) -> Y_pre, Y_post`. Under
  randomization these are not arrows into A.
- `Drought(Jul 2025) -> Y_post` in both arms. Disputed: `Drought × A`
  modification of the effect.
- `Turnover -> observed (R)`. Disputed: `A -> R` (reports changing who stays)
  and `Y -> R`.
- Absent-edge assumptions: no arrow from one town's A to another town's Y
  (no between-town interference), and no arrow from the analyst's choices to A.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Rand[Random draw] --> A[Town arm A]
    A --> Mail[Monthly report mailed]
    Mail --> Read[Read / engaged - unobserved]
    Read --> Y[Use Mar25-Feb26]
    Mail --> Rebate[Rebate sign-up]
    Rebate --> Y
    U[Conservation-mindedness - unobserved] --> Rebate
    U --> Ypre[Use Mar23-Feb25]
    U --> Y
    X[HH size, lot size - pre t0] --> Ypre
    X --> Y
    D[Drought order Jul25 - all towns] --> Y
    Y -.-> R[Read/account observed]
    A -.-> R
```

**Proposed adjustment set:** none is needed for identification, because A is
randomized. For precision only: the household's pre-period use (same calendar
months, Mar 2024–Feb 2025; optionally Mar 2023–Feb 2024), household size and
lot size (if pre-t0), and randomization strata if any. These are all
pre-treatment, so including them cannot block the effect.

**Excluded:**
- *Rebate sign-up* is a post-treatment mediator. Conditioning on it removes
  the rebate pathway from the total effect. It is also a collider on
  A → Rebate ← U → Y, which would create bias in the remaining comparison.
- *Post-t0 household size or lot size updates* are excluded for the same reason.
- *Drought* is a period, not a variable to adjust. The randomized contrast
  already nets it out.

**Design restrictions not encoded in the graph:** the randomization itself
(each 12-of-24 assignment equally likely), stable town membership of
households, and no differential outcome measurement by arm.

## 4. Identification assumptions and evidence

| Assumption | Why needed | Supporting evidence | Planned challenge/sensitivity | Untestable remainder or unresolved gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Random assignment of towns as recorded | Exchangeability of arms | Partner reports a random draw | Obtain the draw record; pre-period balance of town mean use, household size and lot size | Gate: record must confirm no post-draw swaps or undocumented re-draws. Balance cannot prove randomization; with 12 per arm, chance imbalance is expected |
| Consistency: one defined intervention | Defines the effect | Monthly mail to all households, no opt-out | Confirm report content versions and any changes after July 2025 | If content changed, the estimand is the effect of the *program as delivered* |
| Outcome measured identically in both arms | No differential measurement | Same smart meters and read system | Compare estimated-read rates and read timing by arm | Unknown until profiled |
| Outcome observation: account turnover unrelated to arm, or handled | Cohort comparability | Meter reads cover all households | Compare turnover and missing-read rates by arm; premise-level sensitivity; bounds if differential | Gate if turnover differs by arm; ignorability of residual missingness is untestable |
| No between-town interference | Control towns represent the no-report scenario | Towns ≥10 miles apart, separate communities | Ask about regional media or social spread | Untestable; spillover would bias the contrast toward zero |
| Positivity/support | Every town could get either arm | By design (complete randomization) | Not applicable | None |
| Few-cluster inference validity | Honest uncertainty (precision, not identification) | 24 clusters, 12 per arm | Randomization inference; small-sample-corrected cluster SEs | With 24 clusters, power may be modest. More reads do not add assignment-level information |

Under these assumptions the 24-town household-average ITT over Mar 2025–Feb
2026 is identified. Identification is not precision: 2.1 million reads
identify the target, but precision is limited by the 24 randomized towns and
the between-town variation. Pre-period adjustment is the main lever on precision.

## 5. Candidate comparison and primary choice

| Candidate | Identified estimand | Match to requested target | Critical assumptions | Required data | Main threat | Feasibility/failure action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Cluster-randomized ITT, baseline-adjusted (ANCOVA), randomization inference** (primary) | 24-town household ITT of mailing, Mar 2025–Feb 2026 | Exact match | Randomization as recorded; no interference; no differential missingness/measurement | Household post-period and pre-period use, arm, town, randomization record | Chance imbalance across only 12+12 towns; one town-specific shock | Feasible now. If the randomization record fails, switch to B with parallel trends as the identifying assumption |
| **B. Two-arm DiD/event study** (household and calendar-month fixed effects, arm × post; monthly event-time coefficients) | Same ITT under randomization. Without valid randomization, the ATT for report towns under parallel untreated trends | Match | Under randomization: as A. As fallback: parallel trends, no anticipation | Same, all 36 months | Under randomization, generally less efficient than ANCOVA when pre/post correlation is imperfect. As fallback, trend divergence | Robustness check for A, and the fallback design. A single adoption date means no staggered-timing problem |
| **C. Analyst's household before/after with covariates and rebate control** | No causal target. A pre/post change mixes the reports, the July 2025 drought order, seasonality and secular trends, with rebate adjustment blocking part of the effect | Does not match | Would need "no other change between periods", which the drought order directly violates | — | Drought, season, trend; a mediator/collider in the adjustment; read-level SEs | Do not use as the causal estimate. It can be reported descriptively as raw change by arm |
| **D. Extension to all 58 towns** | Effect in non-trial towns | Different population | Transport: effect modifiers measured and supported; non-smart-meter towns comparable | Modifier data for the 34 towns; monthly use there may be unavailable | Smart-meter selection correlates with town traits | Not identified now. Needs a transport analysis or a new randomized rollout |

**Primary:** A. **Robustness and fallback:** B. **Weakest assumption:** that
the randomization was carried out and recorded as described, plus
non-differential turnover. With only 12 towns per arm, the main practical
threat is chance imbalance, not confounding. Pre-period adjustment and
leave-one-town-out checks address it.

Sources: Hernán and Robins (2020); Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) for DiD
assumptions in the fallback.

## 6. Diagnostic, falsification and sensitivity plan

All checks are **planned**; none has been performed.

| Check | Data needed | Assumption it can challenge | Limitation | Action if it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization record audit | Draw record, method, strata, any substitutions | Random assignment | Cannot detect undocumented re-draws | Status → `conditional`; use B with parallel trends |
| Pre-period balance (town mean use Mar 2024–Feb 2025, household size, lot size, account counts) | Pre-period data | Implementation of randomization; data errors | Imbalance under 12+12 is expected by chance; balance proves nothing about unobservables | Rely on baseline adjustment; report imbalance; investigate data linkage if extreme |
| Placebo "effect" in the pre-period (fake t0 = March 2024, using Mar 2023–Feb 2024 as baseline) | Pre-period data | Data/merge errors; pre-existing arm differences in trends | Low power with 24 clusters | Investigate data; report as a limitation |
| Event-time profile (monthly arm contrasts, all 36 months) | All reads | Anticipation; timing of onset | Visual; no single test certifies anything | Re-examine time zero and first-mailing timing |
| Turnover and missing/estimated-read rates by arm and month | Account dates, read flags | Outcome observation | Equal rates do not prove ignorable missingness | Premise-level analysis; inverse-probability-of-observation weighting with a defended model; bounds |
| Premise-level ITT (service address, any occupant) | Premise IDs | Cohort definition | Different estimand (premises, not households) | Report alongside; explain divergence |
| Leave-one-town-out | Town-level data | Undue influence of a town-specific shock | Descriptive only | Report range; inventory events in influential towns |
| Outlier sensitivity (winsorized outcome, prespecified percentile) | Household outcomes | Influence of extreme users / leaks | Winsorizing changes the estimand | Report as secondary; primary stays untrimmed |
| Negative-control outcome (if available, e.g., a metered non-household account class not mailed reports) | Non-residential reads in same towns | Arm-level shocks unrelated to reports | Spillovers to such accounts possible | Investigate shocks |
| Interference inquiry (regional media coverage, control-town awareness) | Communications records | No interference | Cannot quantify spillover precisely | Interpret estimate as a lower bound on the no-spillover effect |
| Rebate sign-up ITT (secondary outcome) | Rebate records | Mechanism plausibility | Not a decomposition of the effect | Report descriptively as a pathway; mediation would need its own design |
| Drought-period split (Mar–Jun vs Jul–Feb effects) | Monthly reads | Effect heterogeneity | Confounded with season; exploratory only | Label as exploratory; no causal claim about drought interaction |

Passing these checks is supporting evidence, not proof. Randomization, not
diagnostics, carries identification.

## 7. Implementation handoff

- **Estimands:** primary is the household-average ITT of town assignment to
  reports, as a difference in mean monthly use (assumed gallons/household/month)
  over Mar 2025–Feb 2026, in the 24 trial towns. Secondary: the percent
  difference (ratio of arm means), monthly event-time contrasts, rebate
  sign-up ITT, and the premise-level ITT. Not estimated: a 58-town effect,
  a reading effect, or a "direct" effect net of rebate.
- **Cohort:** households (accounts) active at the end of February 2025 in the
  24 towns. Outcome = mean of their available monthly reads in the post-period,
  normalized by consumption days. Households joining after t0 go to the
  premise-level sensitivity only. Missing/estimated reads are flagged, not dropped silently.
- **Keys and roles:** town (cluster, assignment unit); account/premise (unit);
  read date and consumption days (time); arm (randomized). Pre-period use from
  the same calendar months a year earlier is the baseline covariate. Household
  size and lot size are covariates only if measured before t0. Rebate is an
  outcome, never a regressor.
- **Primary estimator:** household-level regression of post-period mean use on
  arm, baseline-year mean use (optionally also Mar 2023–Feb 2024),
  household size, lot size and strata if any. Estimate the arm coefficient
  with household weights. Also report the unadjusted arm contrast and a
  town-level analysis (24 town means of residualized use) for transparency.
- **Inference:**
  - Randomization inference over all C(24,12) = 2,704,156 possible assignments,
    or respecting strata if any. Enumeration is feasible. The test statistic
    is the prespecified adjusted arm contrast. Confidence intervals come from
    test inversion under a constant additive effect, with that assumption stated.
  - Also report cluster-robust standard errors at the town level with a
    small-sample correction (e.g., CR2 with reduced degrees of freedom) or a
    wild cluster bootstrap.
  - Do not report read- or household-level i.i.d. standard errors.
  - Primary-source citations for few-cluster inference methods should be
    verified and added before the analysis plan is finalized; none are cited
    here.
- **Robustness:** candidate B (two-arm DiD with household and month fixed
  effects; arm × post; event-time coefficients), plus the §6 sensitivities.
- **Gates (stop before estimation if unresolved):** randomization record;
  first-mailing date versus March read timing; turnover and estimated-read
  definitions; timing of covariate measurement. Stop, and switch to B as the
  identifying design, if the draw was not followed.
- **Prespecification:** freeze the outcome definition, cohort, covariates,
  test statistic and secondary outcomes before unblinding post-period arm
  contrasts. Limit multiplicity by declaring one primary outcome.
- **Tools:** data profiling in Polars from a warehouse extract. Bayesian
  execution is `not applicable` as primary, because randomization inference
  answers the question directly. An optional hierarchical model could be added
  later via `recommend-probabilistic-model`; it would not change identification.
- **Outputs:** the ITT with randomization-based CI and p-value; the unadjusted
  contrast; the event-time plot; balance and turnover tables; sensitivity
  ranges; rebate ITT. State plainly that the effect applies to the 24
  smart-meter towns in a drought year, not to all 58 towns or other years.

## 8. Sources

- Hernán, M. A., and Robins, J. M. (2020). *Causal Inference: What If.*
  https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook. Used for ITT, randomization,
  exchangeability, mediators/colliders and selection.
- Callaway, B., and Sant'Anna, P. H. C. (2021). *Difference-in-Differences with
  Multiple Time Periods.* https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09015. Used for the DiD
  assumptions in the fallback.
- Official `did` vignette: https://bcallaway11.github.io/did/articles/multi-period-did.html
  (fallback implementation pointer).
- Not yet cited: primary sources for few-cluster inference (randomization
  inference, wild cluster bootstrap, CR2). Verify these before the final plan.

## 9. Open questions and next action

| Question | Who/what can answer | Effect on recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| How exactly was the draw done? Strata or pairs? Any towns swapped or re-drawn? | Trial lead; randomization record | Confirms primary status; strata change inference; swaps move to the DiD fallback |
| Date of the first mailing versus March 2025 read dates | Mailing log, billing system | Sets time zero; March may belong to the pre-period |
| Did report content change during the year (e.g., drought messaging, rebate promotion)? | Program staff | Defines the intervention version; rebate promotion makes that pathway explicitly part of the treatment |
| Did control towns receive any differential messaging or media coverage about the reports? | Communications staff | Interference; bias toward zero |
| When were household size and lot size recorded? | Billing data owner | Covariate eligibility |
| Account turnover and estimated-read rules | Billing data owner | Cohort, missingness gate |
| Town-specific 2025 events (rate changes, outages, local campaigns, drought enforcement differences) | Operations | Sensitivity interpretation |
| Is the board's decision limited to the 24 towns or about all 58? | Board / management | If all 58, a transport analysis or a randomized rollout is needed |
| Outcome unit and preferred scale (gallons vs percent) | Board / analyst | Primary scale |

**Next action:** obtain the randomization record and the data definitions
above, update this memo, then implement it in a fresh session using this memo
as the specification.
```

**Questions for you** (listed in §9 of the memo, repeated here):

- How was the draw done? Were towns grouped first, and were any re-drawn or swapped?
- When did the first report go out, relative to the March 2025 meter reads?
- Did the report content change during the year, for example drought messages or promoting the rebate?
- Did the control towns see any coverage of the reports?
- When were household size and lot size recorded?
- How do you handle households that move, and estimated reads?
- Is the board's decision about these 24 towns or about all 58?
